items.title: Knicks Sign Kevin McCullar, Tyler Nickel To Two-Way Contracts
items.summary: The New York Knicks have re-signed guard Kevin McCullar to a two-way contract. The Knicks also signed 2026 second-round pick Tyler Nickel to a two-way contract. McCullar spent last season with New York on a two-way deal. In 14 G League games with the Westchester Knicks last season, the 6-foot-6 guard averaged 16.8 points, 5.7 rebounds, 6.0 assists, 1.9 steals and a block per game. Nickel was selected with the 47th pick in the 2026 NBA Draft out Vanderbilt. The 6-foot-7 forward averaged 13.5 points on 45/40/85 shooting splits and 3.2 rebounds per as a senior for the Commodores. Nickel had been in a legal battle with the NCAA over the ability to return to college for fifth season of eligibility. Now, Nickel will instead begin his NBA career on a two-way deal with the defending champions.

items.title: Knicks Sign N'Faly Dante To Exhibit 10 Contract
items.summary: The New York Knicks signed big man N'Faly Dante to an Exhibit 10 contract. Dante will join a group competing for a roster spot. The 6-foot-11 forward/center is eligible to have his deal converted to a two-way contract. Dante tore his right ACL in late December last season. Prior to that, he had appeared in four games for the Atlanta Hawks. Dante was later waived in order for Atlanta to create a roster spot to complete trade deadline moves. In the G League, Dante has proven to be a good finisher around the rim, solid rebounder and strong rim protector. The Knicks still have one two-way spot open, as well as two standard spots on their regular season roster. New York is likely to only fill one standard spot initially, in order to stay under the second apron.

items.title: Miles McBride 'A Little Disappointed' In How Extension Talks Have Gone With Knicks
items.summary: New York Knicks guard Miles McBride wants to stay with the only NBA teams he's ever played for. That desire is why McBride wishes extension talks with the Knicks were going better. "I love being in New York. Obviously, I've been here my whole career," McBride told The New York Daily News. "I'm a little - I'm a little disappointed. Of course, you want to obviously come to the right terms, and I want to be in New York. So yeah, it's a little hard at times, but I'm gonna be a professional. I want to go out and do my job. So that's in my ability, and to help the team win for as long as I'm with the team." McBride feels that whenever he's had the opportunity, he's showed what he can do on the floor. The sixth-year guard feels he's got even more room to grow too. "I feel like in times where guys have been out, I've been able to show a lot," McBride said. "So it's always - to me - it's about opportunity. I feel like I've continued to grow and improve every single year."
